title: What happened in AI — Sep 19, 2026
intro: Today's signal is speed and trust in coding agents. A new agent tool called Jev already has at least six clones two days after its debut, while LinkedIn and Databricks published production approaches to keeping agents grounded and monitored at scale.

On the risk side, Zhipu's ZCode faces accusations of silently uploading full code histories, and SwarmAuth ships an OAuth 2.1 standard built for agent swarms — both signs that auth and provenance for coding agents are becoming urgent, not optional.
highlights: A coding-agent tool called Jev spawned at least six clones within two days, including a Rust port (S1Code).
LinkedIn detailed an MCP-based context layer that gives its coding agents procedural memory across large codebases.
Databricks published RADAR, an anomaly-detection method for catching monitoring-invisible "gray failures."
Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash now undercuts Gemini Flash on price while matching its multimodal benchmarks.
SwarmAuth brings OAuth 2.1 to multi-agent swarms, while Zhipu's ZCode faces accusations of silently exfiltrating full code histories.
